messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — elevated 5xx and connection reset counts observed from us-west-2 AZ az1d. Auto-pager sent to #incidents and infra-oncall.

alice.k: seeing a sudden jump in inference tail latency from hosts in az1d, looks like lots of `ECONNRESET` and `ENETUNREACH` in kernel logs. Affected G5 pools in that zone. Customers with AZ pinning impacted.

ben.s: confirming metrics: overall 5xx rate for inference fleet +API is ~3% in last 5m but for requests routed to az1d it's ~18%. Error steam: `502` + `upstream reset`. Token throughput dropped ~40% on a subset of hosts.

carla-rte: created bridge: https://call.example.com/infra-2371112222 — joining now. Adding incident runbook link: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/az-network-deg.json 

dave_infra: quick traceback from one node:```
Mar 15 12:01:21 host-g5-043 kernel: enic0: tx timeout, resetting
Mar 15 12:01:22 host-g5-043 systemd: Pod xxxxxx reported ELB connection reset
Mar 15 12:01:24 inference-runtime: kvcache: failed to fetch prefix, upstream econnreset
```
Looks like host NICs in az1d are flapping. Not seeing CPU/GPU pressure.

infra-oncall: I've muted noisy alerts and pinned the dashboard to only show az1d vs others. Opening AWS support case now. Routing/mitigation options: 1) steer traffic away from az1d at LB/Route layer; 2) scale up capacity in adjacent AZs and warm warm-pool; 3) temporarily failover customers pinned to az1d to fallback model variant.

alice.k: can we do an immediate LB-level exclusion? We have per-AZ target groups for the regional ALB. If we remove the az1d target group the ALB should stop sending new connections there. That will cause in-flight errors but stop new hits.

ben.s: agree. Plan: (A) remove AZ target group from ALB, (B) increase capacity in az1b and az1c by +15% using reserved pool, (C) update routing policy in the control plane to prefer non-az1d for inference.

carla-rte: doing ALB change now — will post when complete.

carla-rte: ALB target group for az1d drained (command used):
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30
aws elbv2 remove-tags --resource-arns arn:aws:... --tag-keys AZ=az1d
```
Started deregistration. Expect ~30-60s for in-flight requests to drain.

dave_infra: ramped up node pool in az1b/1c: `infractl scale pool --pool inference-g5 --zone az1b --count +6` and same for az1c. Warm pools now warming.

alice.k: switched model routing policy for pinned customers: fallback to smaller quantized variant `redwood/gptx-q4f` for routes pinned to az1d to reduce request failures while we stabilize. Applied via: `redwoodctl rollout set --route r/enterprise-prod --fallback-model redwood/gptx-q4f --scope az=az1d`

ben.s: metrics after ALB drain + scale: 5xx for region down to 2.1% overall, az1d still at ~7% for legacy pinned requests but trending down. Latency p95 across region back to normal for non-pinned traffic.

infra-oncall: AWS support case opened: case# 12304567231 — assigned to networking team, initial note: "ENA/ENI drops observed for multiple instances in us-west-2a (az1d) causing TCP resets and packet loss." Asked for any maintenance or fabric changes.

aws-support-bot: Support update (12:37 UTC): "Investigating. Observed host-level network interface resets correlated with hypervisor-level interrupt storms. Will escalate to network ops. No planned maintenance."

sean-eng: we should notify affected customers with pinned AZs. Can we compile list of routes/customers currently pinned to az1d and estimate error rates?

alice.k: pulling list now. Quick estimator: ~12 routes pinned, 4 customers showing >10% failed request rate in the last 10m. I'll assemble a short customer impact blurb.

carla-rte: put a short note on status page: "Partial degradation in us-west-2 (single AZ) affecting customers with AZ pinning. We're rerouting traffic and working with cloud provider. Expect intermittent 5xx for some requests."

dave_infra: digging into host-level logs: found repeated `eni attach`/`eni detach` around same time on a subset of hosts. Suspect control-plane attach rate throttling or host interface driver glitch.

ben.s: decision checkpoint: do we declare this Sev2? Impact is limited to a subset of customers but regionally visible. I'm leaning Sev2 due to degraded SLA for some enterprise routes.

infra-oncall: declaring Sev2. Notifying support rotation and paging SRE lead @eva.m.

eva.m: joining bridge. taking lead for next steps. Primary: coordinate long-lived mitigation (rehome pinned customers, confirm AWS mitigation), secondary: postmortem owner.

eva.m: action items assigned: 
- carla: keep ALB excluded until AWS confirms fabric health
- dave: continue host investigations and gather core dumps/logs
- alice: customer impact blurb + outreach list
- ben: monitor traffic shift metrics and rollback plan if errors spike

carla-rte: ALB still draining but new connections from region are no longer going to az1d. Noticing 429s drop and overall error rate improving.

alice.k: customer impact note drafted: "We're experiencing partial single-AZ network degradation in us-west-2 impacting customers with AZ pinning. We've rerouted new traffic away from the affected AZ, scaled capacity in adjacent AZs, and applied temporary model fallbacks for pinned routes. We're working with AWS support to remediate underlying host NIC instability. If you're seeing repeated 5xx, contact support and we'll prioritize rehome. Estimated affected requests <3% of global traffic, ~50% of those are from pinned enterprise routes."

dave_infra: collected host diagnostics tarball and uploaded to S3: `s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2371112222/host-logs.tar.gz`. Shared with AWS case.

aws-support-bot: Support update (12:58 UTC): "We see elevated interrupt rates on rack switch 10.12.124.0 corresponding to az1d hosts. Network ops investigating fabric-level packet drops. Will advise when fabric cleared. Recommended to keep traffic steered away until confirmed."

ben.s: current status: region errors 1.7%, az1d pinned traffic errors ~5% and falling. No evidence of model corruption; KV cache warm misses from retries caused extra load but now stabilizing.

infra-oncall: recommendation: keep exclusion in place for 3 hours after AWS confirms stabilization, then do a controlled re-enable with canary traffic (1% then ramp).

eva.m: handing off operational lead to ben.s for the next 2 hours. ben, you'll run the canary when AWS gives go. I'll own the postmortem.

ben.s: ack — taking lead. I'll post updates and run the canary plan: `infractl canary-reenable --zone az1d --percent 1 --monitor 10m --rollback-on >1% increase in 5xx`.

alice.k: outreach sent to affected customers with mitigation steps and expected timeline. No major customer escalations yet, one enterprise partner flagged higher-than-usual latency; we prioritized their route rehome.

carla-rte: leaving ALB exclusion in place for now. Will not re-enable until confirmed.

dave_infra: continuing collection of kernel traces and will attach to support case. Not seeing instance health-check failures at hypervisor level yet (hosts still show healthy in console but NIC errors present).

aws-support-bot: Support update (13:32 UTC): "Network ops replaced affected spine port and cleared error counters. Recommend monitoring for 30-60 minutes and, if stable, reintroduce hosts gradually."

ben.s: will wait 30m then run 1% canary if no regressions. If stable, ramp to 10% then 50% over 45m.

eva.m: postmortem owner noted. Keep logs and timeline in the incident channel. I'll schedule a 1-hour writeup session in 24h.

infra-oncall: final note: major mitigations executed: ALB AZ exclusion, pool scale-up, model fallback for pinned routes, AWS escalated fabric ops. Monitoring continues.

sean-eng: thanks team. keep updates concise in channel.

alice.k: closing bridge in 10m unless new regressions.

carla-rte: bridge closed. leaving thread for follow-ups and postmortem actions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — AWS reported fabric cleared and no further NIC resets observed. Az1d re-enable planned with canary per runbook.

ben.s: re-enable complete at 14:35 UTC after canary ramp — no regression. Marking incident as mitigated.

eva.m: filing postmortem and next steps: investigate autoscaling fallback for AZ pinning, improve customer rehome automation, tighten telemetry for ENI attach errors.

alice.k: thanks all.
